name: Sculptra buttock injections

card.summary: Injections of poly-L-lactic acid (Sculptra) into the buttocks that stimulate collagen over weeks to add gradual volume and contour without surgery.
card.note: Buttock use is off-label in the US; nodules are a reported side effect.

quick.overview:
Sculptra buttock injections use poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA), a biodegradable polymer that prompts the body to build collagen, to add gradual fullness and smoother contour to the buttocks. Unlike fillers that add volume immediately, results build over several weeks to months.

Sculptra is FDA-approved for facial uses, and buttock treatment is described as off-label. A small registered phase 4 trial (NCT03922464, 30 participants, started 2019) evaluated PLLA for buttock contouring and lifting [1].
quick.how: Treatment is performed by a clinician in an office setting, usually as a series of sessions several weeks apart, with results said to last up to about two years [2].
quick.risks: Common effects are swelling, bruising, redness and tenderness; lumps under the skin occur less often, and a 2015 study cited a nodule rate of 7 to 9 percent linked to injection depth [2]. Off-label status means the approved product information does not cover this use.

lead: Sculptra is an injectable containing poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) that stimulates collagen production rather than adding volume directly [2][3]. Used in the buttocks, it is described as a non-surgical way to add fullness, smooth cellulite dimpling and refine contour.

Healthline lists nonsurgical buttock augmentation among Sculptra's off-label uses, with results building over weeks to months and lasting up to two years [2]. A registered phase 4 trial (NCT03922464) titled "Efficacy and Safety of Poly-L-lactic Acid" studied buttock contouring and lifting in 30 participants [1].

angle.text: PLLA is injected to build collagen over weeks, gradually raising buttock volume and smoothing the surface. People choose it for shape change without implants or fat transfer.

paras: PLLA is a biodegradable synthetic polymer. After the carrier is absorbed, the particles are recognised as foreign, recruiting macrophages and fibroblasts and increasing collagen, which provides gradual rather than immediate volume [3].

Sculptra was FDA-approved in 2004 for facial fat loss in people with HIV and later for facial wrinkles and folds [2]. Buttock augmentation, cellulite and body contouring are listed as off-label uses [2]. The average regimen for the face is about three sessions over three to four months [2].
A registered phase 4 trial, NCT03922464, evaluated efficacy and safety of PLLA for buttock contouring and lifting in 30 participants, started April 2019 and listed as completed [1].

Common effects include swelling, bruising, redness, tenderness, pain, bleeding and itching, usually subsiding within days; lumps and skin discolouration are less common [2]. Filler risks in general include infection and allergic reactions that may need surgical correction [3].

timeline.event: FDA approval of Sculptra for facial lipoatrophy in HIV [2]
Phase 4 trial of PLLA for buttock contouring begins [1]
